summary: The enterprise AI model API landscape in 2026 is dominated by hyperscaler aggregators that let corporations consume multiple foundation models (Claude, GPT, Llama, Mistral, Gemini, and more) through a single managed API while keeping data inside their own cloud security perimeter. There is no single winner — AWS Bedrock leads on model breadth, Azure OpenAI on OpenAI-native depth and Microsoft integration, and Google Vertex AI on Gemini and ML tooling — with data-platform players like Snowflake Cortex and Databricks bringing models to where enterprise data already lives. Selection is driven primarily by existing cloud footprint, compliance requirements, and the unit of capacity/throughput each platform reserves.
why_enterprises_use_aggregators: Data residency and security: prompts, context, and fine-tuning data stay within the company's own VPC/region and are not sent to a third-party vendor API, satisfying internal and regulatory data-handling rules.
Compliance and governance: aggregators provide ready-made SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, FedRAMP, and GDPR coverage plus centralized audit logs, IAM, and content filtering that raw vendor APIs often lack.

Single billing and existing cloud contracts: usage rolls into existing enterprise agreements and committed spend (EDP/MACC), consolidating procurement, invoicing, and discounts rather than managing many separate vendor relationships.
Model choice and avoiding lock-in: one API exposes many competing models (Claude, Llama, Mistral, Cohere, Gemini, Nova), letting teams swap or route between models without re-architecting.

Integration with enterprise data and tooling: native connectivity to the cloud's storage, vector databases, identity, networking, and MLOps pipelines makes RAG, fine-tuning, and agent deployment faster and more secure.

platforms.name: AWS Bedrock
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-token (on-demand) plus Provisioned Throughput; capacity reserved in model units with batch and commitment discounts.
platforms.best_for: Enterprises already on AWS wanting the widest choice of third-party models behind one API.

platforms.name: Azure OpenAI Service
available_models: (via Azure AI Foundry) Llama, Mistral, Cohere
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go per token plus Provisioned Throughput Units (PTUs) for reserved, predictable capacity.
key_features: Private networking via VNet and Private Endpoints
Azure Monitor and diagnostic audit logs
platforms.best_for: Microsoft-first shops needing deep OpenAI model access with enterprise governance and Copilot/M365 integration.

platforms.name: Google Vertex AI Model Garden
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-token on-demand plus Provisioned Throughput sold in GSUs (Generative AI Scale Units); 25 GSUs of Gemini 2.5 Flash gives roughly 67,250 tokens/sec sustained.
key_features: VPC Service Controls and Private Service Connect
Grounding with Google Search and RAG engine
platforms.best_for: Data/ML-heavy teams on Google Cloud wanting Gemini plus strong ML tooling and multi-model access.

platforms.name: Snowflake Cortex AI
platforms.pricing: Consumption-based using Snowflake credits, billed per token/compute within the Snowflake account.
key_features: Models run inside the Snowflake data perimeter (no data movement)
Access logging and governance via Snowflake Horizon
Cortex Analyst and Cortex Search (RAG) over governed data
platforms.best_for: Organizations centralizing analytics in Snowflake that want LLMs directly on their governed data.

platforms.name: IBM watsonx.ai
platforms.pricing: Subscription and consumption-based (Resource Units); available on IBM Cloud, on-premises, and hybrid.
key_features: watsonx.governance for audit, risk and lineage
watsonx Orchestrate for cross-platform AI agent management
platforms.best_for: Regulated enterprises needing hybrid/on-prem deployment, strong AI governance, and agent orchestration.

platforms.name: Databricks Mosaic AI
platforms.pricing: Consumption-based (DBUs) for model serving, fine-tuning, and training within the Databricks Lakehouse.
key_features: Model serving inside the customer's cloud/VPC
Vector Search and RAG on lakehouse data
platforms.best_for: Data engineering/ML teams building custom and fine-tuned models on top of a governed lakehouse.

platforms.name: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Generative AI
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-use (per character/token) plus dedicated AI clusters for reserved capacity.
key_features: Private endpoints and OCI networking isolation
Tight integration with Oracle apps and databases
platforms.best_for: Oracle-centric enterprises wanting managed GenAI near their Oracle databases and applications.

platforms.name: Cloudflare Workers AI
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-use ('Neurons' / per request and token); low entry cost with serverless edge billing.
key_features: Serverless inference at the global edge (low latency)
AI Gateway for caching, rate limiting and observability
Integration with Workers, R2, and Vectorize (RAG)
platforms.best_for: Developers and enterprises needing low-latency, globally distributed open-model inference at the edge.
